$comment: Gate 1 (devolt memory/decisions/2026-09-25-brownout-core-w1-plan.md, section
3.4.1; core/README.md's contract). Every test case in every suite file
wired into vitest.core-suites.config.ts's `test.include` is listed here,
classified as one of:
- "portable":     runs on the core for the kinds it uses; wired into
vitest.core-suites.config.ts's testNamePattern.
- "classic-only":  pins a classic-internal detail (step counts, Newton
iteration counts, engine.state, captureErrorState,
a split) that has no core counterpart and is not
part of the accuracy contract; never runs on the core.
- "not-yet":       every kind the test's circuit uses is real device
behaviour, but at least one of those kinds has not
been ported to the core yet (or, for a handful of
kinds below, is not in the W1 plan's kind table at
all -- diode/bjt_npn/nmos/lm358/microbit).
`kinds` lists every SimComponent.kind the test's circuit instantiates
(excluding the implicit ground net). gate-reporter.ts sums, per kind, how
many "portable" cases actually ran and passed under this file's
testNamePattern, and fails the whole run if any kind named in a portable
case's `kinds` array has a count of zero for that file -- see its own
header comment for why this must be computed from portable entries only,
not from CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS (which also contains "ground", a compiler-
internal detail no test ever names as a component kind). It ALSO fails
when any CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS member except "ground" has no portable
case, in any file, that ran and passed (the coverage floor, W1b review
finding 9): a kind the core implements must be exercised here.

cases.reason: Reconstructs `capacitorCurrent = capacitance * (voltage - previousVoltage) / h` and checks a KCL residual against it -- a property of classic's own fixed-h backward-Euler finite difference, not of the device's continuous physics. The core's single-capacitor partition (W1b step 2) advances the closed form continuously (no per-step h to reconstruct a matching discrete derivative from), so this identity is not a like-for-like comparison there. A future worker could add that passthrough (HeadlessRunnerOptions.compileOptions, threaded into CoreEngine.load's options) to lift this to "portable" under FORCE_STEPPED.

cases.reason: com is fixed (wired directly to the source) and b is the device's only OTHER free pin (c has no wire to it either in this case's own rig, since r1 sits on c) -- wait, r1 is wired to c even here, so b and c are the device's two free contacts in potentially different partitions (com fixed, so nothing unions them, per finding 1). cases.describe: capacitor ESR + leakage backward-Euler companion
cases.name: applies exact catalog ESR/leakage defaults to an older identified save
cases.reason: This fixture's capacitor sits directly across the ideal source (c.a to src.pos, c.b to src.neg) -- BOTH terminals are fixed nodes, and rule 2a (core/README.md) now gives the core an exact closed form for exactly this topology instead of declining it, so the old topology block is gone. But this specific test is not a rule-2a check: it hand-computes ONE deliberately huge backward-Euler step (h=0.5s against esr=1, C=1F -- h/(esr*C) = 0.5, half of tau) and asserts classic's OWN single-step companion value, series 5/(1+0.5/1) = 3.3333333333333335 A plus leakage 5/1e7 = 5e-7 A, total 3.3333338333333336 A. Verified empirically by temporarily marking this case portable: the core reports the mathematically exact rule-2a answer instead -- series 5*exp(-0.5) = 3.0326532985631669 A plus the same 5e-7 A leakage, total 3.032653798563167 A (bit-identical to `fixedPairCapacitorCurrentAt(5, 1, 1, 1e7, 0.5)`, test/core/equivalence/analytic.ts) -- which differs from classic's crude one-step approximation by 0.30068 A, about 9% of the expected value and six orders of magnitude past this test's 5e-8 `toBeCloseTo` bound. This is not the load-instant/first-step artifact rule 2a's README bullet documents (that is specific to esr=0); it is classic's own large-step discretisation error at a genuinely non-ideal esr, which the core is BY DESIGN more accurate than. Reclassifying this exact assertion portable would require either the core to reproduce classic's inexact single-step arithmetic (wrong direction for W1b) or loosening this test's own tolerance (which this worker does not own and must not do to force a pass) -- so it stays classic-only, for a materially different reason than before.

cases.describe: 74HC14 — Schmitt hysteresis dead band
cases.name: holds LOW output when input is in dead band approached from above
cases.reason: Empirically fails on the built core: expected the output to stay LOW across the reload (the Schmitt-held input level carried forward from before), got the opposite. core/README.md rule 5 (Kernel semantics: partitions and dynamic solves) states plainly that "carrying charge across a reload is W2" for capacitors; the same is true for a digital IC's per-pin Schmitt hold-state and in-flight delay-FSM timers (classic's icState, sim-engine.ts:1043's own comment: "74HC14 icState carries per-input Schmitt hysteresis level"; carried forward by component id at every classic load(), sim-engine.ts:2808) — bo_engine_load has no per-id state carry-forward at all in W1, so every reload starts the IC's Schmitt/delay state fresh. This is a known, explicitly-documented W1 limitation (load carry-forward is W2, decision 1), not a core bug; not-yet until W2 lands.

cases.describe: 74HC14 — Schmitt hysteresis dead band
cases.name: holds HIGH output when input is in dead band approached from below
cases.reason: Passes on the built core TODAY, but only by coincidence, not because the mechanism is correct: with no reload carry-forward (see the "approached from above" sibling case's reason — core/README.md rule 5, "carrying charge across a reload is W2", generalised to digital IC state), a freshly-reloaded IC's Schmitt hold-state defaults to LOW (core/README.md rule 4, "in between it holds its per-pin state (default LOW)"), which happens to equal the state this direction of approach needs anyway. Classifying this "portable" would be exactly the vacuous/coincidental pass gate 1's own no-silent-fallback design (adapter.ts's header, section 3.6 risk 3) exists to catch: it is not proving digital identity for the right reason, and would silently stop proving anything the day the default or classic's own default diverge. not-yet, for the same W2 load-carry-forward reason as its sibling.

cases.describe: 74LS47 — Schmitt commit semantics (74HC14)
cases.name: dead-band input from above: output stays LOW across 20 steps
cases.reason: Empirically fails on the built core: expected the output to stay LOW across the reload (the Schmitt-held input level carried forward from before), got the opposite. core/README.md rule 5 (Kernel semantics: partitions and dynamic solves) states plainly that "carrying charge across a reload is W2" for capacitors; the same is true for a digital IC's per-pin Schmitt hold-state and in-flight delay-FSM timers (classic's icState, sim-engine.ts:1043's own comment: "74HC14 icState carries per-input Schmitt hysteresis level"; carried forward by component id at every classic load(), sim-engine.ts:2808) — bo_engine_load has no per-id state carry-forward at all in W1, so every reload starts the IC's Schmitt/delay state fresh. This is a known, explicitly-documented W1 limitation (load carry-forward is W2, decision 1), not a core bug; not-yet until W2 lands.

cases.describe: 74LS47 — Schmitt commit semantics (74HC14)
cases.name: dead-band input from below: output stays HIGH across 20 steps
cases.reason: Passes on the built core TODAY, but only by coincidence, not because the mechanism is correct: with no reload carry-forward (see the "approached from above" sibling case's reason — core/README.md rule 5, "carrying charge across a reload is W2", generalised to digital IC state), a freshly-reloaded IC's Schmitt hold-state defaults to LOW (core/README.md rule 4, "in between it holds its per-pin state (default LOW)"), which happens to equal the state this direction of approach needs anyway. Classifying this "portable" would be exactly the vacuous/coincidental pass gate 1's own no-silent-fallback design (adapter.ts's header, section 3.6 risk 3) exists to catch: it is not proving digital identity for the right reason, and would silently stop proving anything the day the default or classic's own default diverge. not-yet, for the same W2 load-carry-forward reason as its sibling.

Does not itself pin the 20 ns delay value (that is classic's own catalog-fallback resolution, consumed identically by the core's own delay param per core/README.md's IC blob per-pin delay field) — and, being merely "defined", it cannot distinguish AND from NAND, OR, or any other committed 2-input function either (review finding 14). The real truth-table proof (both LOW, one HIGH, and — the row that actually distinguishes AND from NAND — both HIGH) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74LS08 quad AND" describe block; this case is left as-is because its own subject (the prop-delay prefix fallback) is unaffected by that gap.

cases.describe: infrastructure — catalog prop_delay_ns override
cases.name: 74hc14 uses catalog-declared prop_delay_ns=15 (same value as prefix default)
cases.reason: Loads with the input already at its final level, so the load-time settle (zero delay, core/README.md's events section: "the first observation has zero delay") resolves 1y before any delay could ever be observed — a catalog delay of 0 ns, 15 ns or 50 us would all pass this case identically (sampled after two 100 us steps, far past any of them). This only proves the gate inverts (the input/output pin mapping and polarity are correct), never that any particular propagation delay is honoured. The genuine observable-delay check (a continuous RC threshold crossing during ordinary step()s, never a reload) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74HC14 Schmitt inverter: a genuinely observed propagation delay" case (review finding 15).

cases.describe: infrastructure — catalog prop_delay_ns override
cases.name: 74ls47 uses catalog-declared prop_delay_ns=35 — output delay observable
cases.reason: Empirically fails on the built core: expected digitalState to still show the OLD committed value 25 ns after a reload changed the BCD input (less than the 35 ns catalog prop delay), got the NEW value already committed. Same root cause as the 74HC14 Schmitt dead-band cases above: bo_engine_load carries no per-id digital state forward (core/README.md rule 5's "carrying charge across a reload is W2", generalised) so the delay FSM treats every pin as a fresh first observation on reload, and "first observation has zero delay" (core/README.md's events section, mirroring classic's own §2.4 rule) commits the new value immediately instead of respecting the in-flight 35 ns timer a live (non-reloaded) transition would get. Not a core bug -- a known, documented W1 limitation (load carry-forward is W2, decision 1). The 74hc14 prop_delay_ns=15 case above does NOT prove the core's own delay-FSM timing either (review finding 15: it loads with the input already at its final level, so its load-time settle resolves before any delay could be observed). combinational-ics.test.ts's "a genuinely observed propagation delay" case (a continuous RC threshold crossing, never a reload — sidestepping this exact W2 gap entirely) is the first case anywhere in this corpus that actually proves the core's delay-FSM timing on a live (non-reloaded) transition, for the 74hc14 kind — 74ls47's own 35 ns value across a RELOAD-based transition specifically is still unverified pending W2's reload carry-forward (this case's own subject).

cases.describe: digital realism — propagation delay
cases.name: holds a 74LS gate output until the package delay has elapsed
cases.reason: After engine.load(circuit), this mutates circuit.components.find(...).params.voltage on the SAME retained JS object WITHOUT calling engine.load() again, relying on classic's load() keeping a live reference (this.circuit = circuit, sim-engine.ts:2445) and re-reading component.params on every subsequent Newton iterate. The core adapter's load() compiles the circuit into a WASM program once; a later in-place mutation of the JS object has no effect on an already-loaded core program (there is no live binding, and Decision 1's toggle mechanism covers only switch/dip 'closed' params, not a voltage_source's voltage). Routing this case through the core would silently keep the OLD input forever and fail its own later assertion (digitalState flipping after the delay) rather than reproduce classic's propagation-delay behaviour — a classic implementation-detail dependency, not a like-for-like core comparison. (The core's own delay-FSM timing is instead proven by the 74ls47 prop_delay_ns case above, which DOES reload.)

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC14 Schmitt inverter: a genuinely observed propagation delay
cases.name: the digital commit lands measurably AFTER 1a crosses the Schmitt threshold — neither immediate (0ns) nor absurdly late (us-scale)
cases.reason: Review finding 15: the pre-existing 74hc14 prop_delay_ns=15 case (wave2-combinational.test.ts) loads with the input already at its final level, so its load-time settle (zero delay) resolves before any delay could be observed. A live RELOAD-based transition (the mechanism wave2-sequential.test.ts's 74HC74 edge tests use) is not usable either: a core reload re-runs decision 8's zero-delay t=0 settle with no per-id carry-forward yet (W2 scope — the same reason this file's own "Schmitt commit semantics"/prop_delay=35ns "not-yet" cases above are not portable), so the new input would commit with NO delay on the core only. This case instead feeds 1a from a plain RC network already present at load time — a genuine continuous analog crossing during ordinary step()s, with no second load() anywhere (the same mechanism fixture 19's relaxation oscillator uses) — and dynamically locates both the analog crossing and the digital commit, asserting the gap between them is bounded to the tens-of-ns ballpark the 15ns catalog value lives in, ruling out both "skipped entirely" and "some unrelated us-scale mechanism".
